name: semantic-crosscheck
description: Cross-layer verification for an ontology plus semantic layer on PostgreSQL 17, for Codex and Claude Code.

interface.shortDescription: Prove that a PostgreSQL closure, SHACL rules, OWL reasoning and a Cube model agree.
interface.longDescription: Release v0.14.0: cross-checks PostgreSQL17 closures, SQL/SHACL rules, OWL/HermiT and Cube against gold SQL. A Cube /load answer outside Cube's load envelope, a body that is not JSON or a gold-query row without a mapped member is now an error instead of zero rows or NULL, so V1/V2 cannot pass vacuously, a V3 pair test cannot pass over no keys and V4 cannot count a false kill. The closure_join_swap mutation witness counts closure pairs whose ends join different measure rows, so witness 0 proves that every query answers the same and observable mutants are served instead of skipped as equivalent. reason --explain-inconsistency reports whether a completed subset-minimal explanation is unique over the generated axiom groups (unique, not_unique or not_proven) with one extra same-HermiT check per retained group. A repeated ontology.no_children value is a configuration error. Same-engine explanation is not independent certification. Dependency pins and defaults stay unchanged. Rerun build, reason, cube, verify and report after upgrading.
defaultPrompt: Use semantic-crosscheck to run the synthetic demo end to end.
Use semantic-crosscheck to verify my crosscheck.toml against PostgreSQL and explain what is not proven.
